project.name: gitvisualise
project.description: Turn any GitHub repo into an interactive, animated, narrated architecture tour: on the website, from the command line, as a Claude Code skill, or as a GitHub Action. Zero dependencies, no API keys.
notes: Nodes are individual source files; edges are static imports found by the scanner.
Not diagrammed: 21 examples files (add them with --include tests,examples,tooling).

nodes.label: Website logic
nodes.summary: The website's brain. Reads a pasted link or a picked repo, shows progress, then plays the resulting tour. It runs entirely in the visitor's browser and writes to the page with textContent only, because repo text is untrusted.

nodes.label: Website page
nodes.summary: The landing page: link box, account repo picker, optional token, progress view, and the sandboxed frame that plays the tour.

nodes.label: CLI
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point. Parses the command (scan, generate, validate, build, all, serve), resolves a local path or GitHub URL, and runs the pipeline in order.

nodes.label: Site builder (disk)
nodes.summary: Node adapter that writes the static site to a folder: index.html plus the viewer script and styles.

nodes.label: Page renderer
nodes.summary: Pure page rendering shared by the CLI and the website: embeds architecture data and code snippets, escapes repo text, adds a no-JavaScript summary, and can inline everything into a single file.

nodes.label: Path helpers
nodes.summary: A minimal POSIX path library so the core code runs in a browser, where node:path does not exist.

nodes.label: Scanner core
nodes.summary: Pure scanner shared by the CLI and the website. Given file paths and a read function, it records facts only: resolved imports, entry points, routes and declared dependencies. Nothing is guessed.

nodes.label: Text helpers
nodes.summary: Tiny pure helpers (escaping, slugs, line counts, GitHub URL normalising) that run in both Node and the browser.

nodes.label: Validator rules
nodes.summary: Pure rules that check architecture.json against a repository view: source paths exist with exact case, line ranges are in bounds, steps reference real nodes and edges, and file paths named in prose exist.

nodes.label: Baseline generator
nodes.summary: Builds a first architecture.json from scan facts: files or packages become nodes, imports become edges, and a walk from the entry point becomes a flow with templated narration.

nodes.label: GitHub cloning (CLI)
nodes.summary: Turns a GitHub URL, owner/repo shorthand or a local path into a directory on disk, shallow-cloning public repos into a cache.

nodes.label: Merge (keeps your edits)
nodes.summary: Merges a fresh baseline into an existing architecture.json by id. Items marked claude, manual or locked, and hand-placed positions, survive regeneration.

nodes.label: Scanner (disk)
nodes.summary: Node adapter: walks a folder, reads files and asks git for the commit, then hands everything to the shared scanner core.

nodes.label: Node helpers
nodes.summary: File-system and git helpers used only in Node: JSON I/O, exact-case path checks, argument parsing.

nodes.label: Validator (disk)
nodes.summary: Node adapter that presents a folder on disk to the validator rules as a read-only view.

nodes.label: Browser GitHub loader
nodes.summary: Analyses a GitHub repo from a browser with no server: two API calls for the commit and file tree, then raw file downloads. It prefers a tour the repo authors published, and otherwise runs the shared scanner, generator and validator.

nodes.label: Tour page template
nodes.summary: HTML shell for the tour: diagram canvas, player controls, narration card and detail panel. The page renderer fills in the data.

nodes.label: Viewer engine
nodes.summary: Generic renderer and playback engine. Lays out nodes, animates flow steps, drives play/pause/step controls, and reads narration aloud with the browser speech synthesizer. It contains no project-specific code.

nodes.label: Site assembler
nodes.summary: Copies the website, the shared core and the viewer into docs/ so GitHub Pages serves one consistent site. CI fails if docs/ is stale.

nodes.label: Viewer styles
nodes.summary: Theme tokens for light and dark mode, responsive layout for phones, and reduced-motion handling.

nodes.label: architecture.json
nodes.summary: The single source of truth: nodes, edges, flows and narration, every entry backed by a source reference. Generated, then curated, then rendered.

nodes.label: Browser speech synthesis
nodes.summary: The Web Speech API built into the browser. It speaks narration with no server, key or cost.

nodes.label: GitHub API + raw files
nodes.summary: api.github.com supplies the commit and file tree; raw.githubusercontent.com supplies file contents. Both allow browser requests, so the site needs no backend.

nodes.label: Claude Code skill
nodes.summary: SKILL.md tells Claude Code how to inspect a repo, write grounded architecture data and narration, validate it, and preserve manual edits.

nodes.label: GitHub Action
nodes.summary: A composite action that runs the CLI in any repo's workflow, so the tour regenerates on every push and can be deployed to Pages.

flows.title: From repo to interactive site (CLI)
flows.description: What happens when Claude Code, or you, run the tool on a project.

steps.title: The skill takes charge
steps.narration: When you ask for an interactive architecture, Claude Code loads the skill. It does not guess: it runs the command line tool one stage at a time and checks each result. The GitHub Action drives the very same tool from a workflow.

steps.title: Find the repository
steps.narration: The tool accepts a local folder or a GitHub address. For a GitHub repo it makes a shallow clone into a cache, so the same steps work on any public repository.

steps.title: Scan for facts
steps.narration: A thin adapter walks the folder and reads files, then the scanner core records what is provably there: which file imports which, where execution starts, and which libraries are declared. These facts are the only raw material for the diagram.

steps.title: Draft a baseline
steps.narration: From those facts the generator drafts nodes, edges and a first walkthrough starting at the entry point. It works with no AI and no API key, and Claude then improves the wording and the relationships.

steps.title: Keep human and Claude edits
steps.narration: Before saving, the merge step compares the draft with any existing file. Anything marked as curated or locked is kept, so regenerating after a code change never wipes out careful work.

steps.title: Check every claim
steps.narration: The validator opens the repository and confirms that every referenced file exists, every line range is real, and every step points at a real component. Anything invented fails here, before it reaches a reader.

steps.title: Build the static site
steps.narration: The builder produces plain files: a page with the data and code snippets inlined, plus the viewer script and styles. There is nothing to install or host beyond static files, so GitHub Pages works.

steps.title: The viewer draws it
steps.narration: In the browser, the viewer reads the embedded data and lays the components out in layers. It knows nothing about this project, which is why the same viewer works for any repository.

steps.title: Play and listen
steps.narration: Press play and each step highlights its components while the browser reads the narration aloud. You can pause, step, change speed, pick a voice, or click any component to see its code.

flows.title: From a pasted link to a tour (website)
flows.description: What the website does, entirely inside your browser, when you paste a GitHub link.

steps.title: You paste a link
steps.narration: You paste a GitHub link, or pick a repository from an account. The page runs entirely in your browser. There is no server of ours in the loop, which is why it costs nothing to host.

steps.title: Ask GitHub for the file tree
steps.narration: The loader makes two requests to the public GitHub API: one to pin the exact commit, and one for the complete file listing. Pinning the commit is what keeps every Open Source link pointing at the code you analysed.

steps.title: Download only what matters
steps.narration: It skips tests, examples, tooling config and anything ignored by the repo, then downloads the shallowest source files first, up to a cap. Files come from raw.githubusercontent.com, which does not count against the API limit.

steps.title: Prefer the authors' own tour
steps.narration: If the repository already publishes a curated tour, the loader uses that instead and checks its references against the real files. If they have drifted, you are told, rather than shown stale claims as fact.

steps.title: The same brain as the CLI
steps.narration: Otherwise the loader runs the very same scanner, generator and validator the command line uses. There is one implementation with two front ends, so the website and the CLI cannot disagree.

steps.title: Build one self-contained page
steps.narration: The page renderer embeds the data and code snippets, escapes anything that came from the repository, and inlines the viewer, producing a single HTML document you can also download.

steps.title: Play it in a sandbox
steps.narration: The tour plays inside a sandboxed frame with no access to the surrounding page. Repository text is untrusted, and if you added a token, this keeps it out of reach of anything a repository could contain.

steps.title: Keep it or share it
steps.narration: Copy a share link that re-runs the analysis for anyone who opens it, or download the finished page and the architecture data. When you want narration written from your actual code, add the skill or the action to your repository.

flows.title: What 1.1 added
flows.description: The request tracing, comparison, language and website additions, and where each one lives.

steps.title: Tracing a request from client to server
steps.narration: A fetch or axios call is only linked to a server route when the HTTP method agrees and every path segment matches, with path parameters as the only wildcards. The generator turns each match into an http edge with evidence on both the call and the route, plus a request tour.

steps.title: Comparing two revisions
steps.narration: The loader analyses both revisions with the same node granularity, and the diff marks each component and relationship as added, removed, changed or same by id. Removed items keep their evidence pinned to the older commit, so nothing is invented.

steps.title: Java and Rust import graphs
steps.narration: Each language plug-in builds an index of the repository once, then resolves an import to a file that really exists. Anything that resolves to nothing is dropped rather than guessed.

steps.title: Caching and shareable links
steps.narration: The website stores each analysed tour in IndexedDB, keyed by commit, so a repeat visit costs one request. Route helpers turn a repository, a folder, a comparison or a tour step into a link and back.

steps.title: Optional sign-in
steps.narration: Signing in with GitHub needs a client secret, so the code-for-token exchange lives in a tiny stateless function that never logs. The site only shows the button when config.js turns it on.

flows.description: Follows import relationships outward from the entry point.

steps.title: Start at app.js
steps.narration: Execution starts at app.js. Entry point: conventional entry filename. Follow the highlighted connections to see how the rest of the code is wired together.

steps.title: app.js → config.js
